citations.anchor: keeps a plain textarea for a field that opted out
citations.why: The `rawHtml` field (admin.widget === 'textarea') renders content-admin's textarea and `control('Raw HTML')` has count 0 — the one exception isWysiwygField makes.

citations.anchor: renders stored HTML as content, not markup
citations.why: The plain `richtext` `body` field (no admin.widget at all) renders the plugin's preview, so the default-claim half holds: a richtext field is claimed with no opt-in.

citations.anchor: keeps the record and its chrome on screen
citations.why: With the field unfolded, the content nav, the Properties rail, the top-bar Save and the record heading are all asserted visible — the 'stays mounted and operable' half, which a dialog could not satisfy.

citations.anchor: takes over the work area with the caret already in the text
citations.why: The tab strip is hidden and `control('Summary')` has count 0 once unfolded — the working area's content was replaced, not covered.

citations.anchor: writes edits back to the form as they are made
citations.why: Typing then leaving the editor (no save, no editor-local commit) leaves the typed text in the form's own preview — the edit reached the entry form through onChange.

citations.anchor: stores the formatting the toolbar applied
citations.why: The saved body is compared with toEqual against the exact expected document, so a meaningful document is handed to the form verbatim.

citations.anchor: treats a node that means something without words as content
citations.why: A document holding only a table, a horizontal rule, or a `callout` (a node the core does not know) reads as non-empty — which only holds if emptiness is an allowlist of what emptiness is, not the negation of a list of meaningful nodes.

citations.anchor: treats the document an emptied editor leaves behind as empty
citations.why: The members of the emptiness list are asserted: a bare doc, a doc holding one empty paragraph, and a paragraph of whitespace text all read empty.

citations.anchor: names the structural problems in a body it is handed
citations.why: The remarks under the document name exactly inspectRichText's two findings for that stored body (a table with no header cells, a heading above the level) — the list is built from the core's inspection, not from a second rule set.

citations.anchor: refuses to save a body a screen reader could not follow
citations.why: An error-severity finding blocks the save: the field error names it and saves.bodies stays empty. The complementary half — a warning does **not** block — is now pinned beside it by 'lets a body with only a warning through', which drives the same action on a body whose only finding is advice.

citations.anchor: refuses a language tag assistive tech would ignore
citations.why: The dialog refuses `fr_FR` and stays open with a BCP-47 error, so the tag never reaches the document — the check the dialog runs is isWellFormedLanguageTag, the same one the save applies.

citations.anchor: refuses a URL the editor would not publish
citations.why: Pins the dialog on both refusals: `javascript:alert(1)` and the protocol-relative `//evil.host/x.png` each show the error and insert no image.

citations.anchor: resizes an image from the keyboard, and stores the width
citations.why: Pins two clauses: a keyboard resize lands in the saved node's `width`, and no `height` is ever stored.

citations.anchor: centres a selected image, and stores where it sits
citations.why: The figure carries data-align="center", the saved image node's align is 'center', and the Alignment menu has no 'Justify' item while media is selected.

citations.anchor: clears the alt when the image is marked decorative
citations.why: Pins the stored half: the saved image carries the real alt value, empty included (alt === '' alongside decorative).

citations.anchor: never saves the record from an overlay’s own form
citations.why: On an existing record, submitting the alt popover, the media URL dialog and the link popover each leave saves.bodies empty with no saved toast — the entry is never saved from a popup. The language dialog is the one popup form not exercised.

citations.anchor: stores an image named by URL
citations.why: The built-in 'by URL' dialog is opened from the Insert ▸ Media menu and is then filled and submitted after the menu has closed — it could not survive that if the menu item mounted it.

citations.anchor: places an asset picked from the Media Library
citations.why: The same for a contributed source: the Media Library picker is driven to completion after the menu that opened it is gone, so the slot's Source is mounted by the toolbar.

citations.anchor: offers the rich-text body to view, not to edit
citations.why: Pins the toolbar clause: the expanded read-only view has no 'Formatting' group at all (count 0). The `region` role, the inert document and 'nothing is written back into the form' are pinned by the case beside it; only the unobservable `autofocus` clause is left (see the `partial` for I-31).

citations.anchor: a translated body claims its own language, expanded or not
citations.why: The unfolded view's surface resolves lang='de' for a localized field, outside the form's Translated group. The 'never for a shared one' half is pinned by 'claims no language for a body that is shared across locales', which the seed's new shared `notes` field made falsifiable.

citations.anchor: returns focus to the field when the editor closes
citations.why: After opening from the keyboard and pressing Done, focus is asserted on the field's own control rather than on <body> — the deferred getElementById(id) restore.

citations.anchor: unfolds one field at a time, and only the one that asked
citations.why: With `Body` unfolded, exactly **one** editing surface exists in the whole page and `control('Summary')` has count 0 — a control that owned its own expansion would leave the form (and every other field's control) mounted under it, and two could be open at once. Unfolding `Summary` afterwards resolves the view from the one name: it carries Summary's value and not Body's.

citations.anchor: mounts the editor only while the field is unfolded, and seeds it at mount
citations.why: The count of `[role=textbox][aria-multiline]` surfaces is 0 collapsed, 1 unfolded, 0 again after Done — a panel kept alive behind a `hidden` attribute would show up. The seeding half: a phrase typed at the caret arrives contiguous and in place, which a controlled `setContent` sync would scramble (every keystroke would write the form's value back and drop the caret at the top); reopening seeds a fresh editor from the form's current value.

citations.anchor: grows a table by one row on Tab, then lets go of the keystroke
citations.why: Driven end to end: caret into the last cell, written in, one Tab adds one row with focus still in the document; three more Tabs walk the empty row it made and the third releases focus with the row count unchanged. Deleting `lastRowHasContent` (or the whole extension) makes the third press append instead — the ORT-165 runaway.

citations.anchor: never lets a toolbar press take the selection it is about to act on
citations.why: Asserted **between mousedown and mouseup**, which is the only moment the suppression is visible: every command in the bar runs `chain().focus()`, so an assertion made after the press cannot tell the two implementations apart. Mid-press the surface is still focused and `getSelection()` still holds the phrase. Both toolbar control shapes are pressed — `ToolbarButton` (Bold) and `ToolbarMenuTrigger` (Text color), which are the only two components the bar is built from; focus is not asserted for the second because the dropdown takes it deliberately.

citations.anchor: lets a body with only a warning through
citations.why: The complementary half, on a fixture whose only finding is a warning (a 'click here' link): the list names it as 'Worth fixing' with no 'Blocks saving' row, and the **same** action the blocking case is refused on sends the save. A regression promoting every finding to error fails here.

citations.anchor: never saves the record from the language dialog either
citations.why: The fourth popup form, which the overlay case never reached. Its own test because Apply needs a live selection, and that is only guaranteed straight after unfolding.

citations.anchor: claims no language for a body that is shared across locales
citations.why: The falsifying half, and the fixture repair it needed: the seed now carries a **shared** (`localized: false`) richtext field, `notes`. On the German row its expanded view resolves `lang='en'` (the admin's own `<html lang>`) while `body` beside it resolves `de` — so a view that set `contentLocale` unconditionally now fails.

citations.anchor: ?.attrs?.['color']
citations.why: The second clause, positively: a colour chosen from the toolbar swatch reaches the saved document as `textStyle` with amber's own value. The paste half stays pinned by `transformPastedHTML`'s own spec.

citations.anchor: opens the body as a passage to read, and takes nothing back from it
citations.why: The remaining clauses, less one: the expanded read-only surface is a labelled `region` (with no `textbox` anywhere on the page), it is `contenteditable="false"`, and keystrokes aimed at it change neither the document nor the collapsed card the form renders from.

citations.anchor: it('stores an emptied editor as null, not as an empty paragraph'
citations.why: The other half, and the one the browser cannot see: content-admin's required check calls isEmptyRichText, which an empty-paragraph document also satisfies, so only the stored shape tells null from a doc with one empty paragraph.

citations.anchor: it('places the admissible ones out of a mixed list'
citations.why: The node's own check on the insert side: insertMedia filters per embed on isSafeMediaSrc, so a picker returning one unusable asset still places the other three and stores no broken node.

citations.anchor: it('is refused by the node, not only by the dialog'
citations.why: The parse side: an editor opened on markup carrying a javascript: and a protocol-relative img keeps only the admissible one and emits no src="" — the parseHTML getAttrs a body written straight through the API meets. Mutating getAttrs to () => null fails it.

citations.anchor: it('reads a width below the floor as no width at all'
citations.why: The parse side of the floor: a stored width="20" reads back as no width rather than being clamped to 64. (The live drag handle does clamp, which is a bound on a gesture rather than on what a width value means.)

citations.anchor: it('reads an embed narrower than the floor as no width chosen'
citations.why: The write side: insertMedia stores null for a below-floor width and 320 for a real one, so a Math.max clamp in its place fails here.

citations.anchor: it('stops writing data-align once the picture goes back to left'
citations.why: Pins that `left` is never written: centring then re-aligning left removes the attribute from the serialized body while the node still knows its alignment. The sibling case pins the parse side (a stored data-align="left" is understood and normalized away).

citations.anchor: it('moves media by its margins, never by text-align'
citations.why: Pins the mechanism: every [data-align] rule in styles.css declares margin-inline and none declares text-align, and no rule exists for left at all. text-align positions a block's inline children, so a stylesheet tidied onto it would move nothing.

citations.anchor: it('is named for the author without inventing one for the reader'
citations.why: The editor-side half, asserted together with the one it must not break: a described image keeps its alt, an un-alt'd one renders 'Embedded image', and the editor's own getHTML still carries alt="" and never the fallback.

citations.anchor: describe('where the caret starts
citations.why: The autofocus clause, reached through the selection rather than through DOM focus: the panel's own editor (via .tiptap's editor back-reference) puts the caret at doc.content.size - 1 when editable and leaves it at 1 when read-only. Flipping the guard to a constant 'end' fails the read-only case.

citations.anchor: it('serializes one document to the same markup'
citations.why: The second clause: a document holding headings, lists, a table, columns, an aligned image and a video serializes byte-for-byte identically through the editor's getHTML and through the preview's renderRichText, with the fixture's own contents asserted so the comparison cannot be vacuous. The sibling case pins the one deliberate difference (links flattened to spans).
